title: Secrets and logs
summary: Keep signing keys and client secrets out of code, and keep tokens and passwords out of your logs.

steps.title: Where secrets live
body: Everything in this topic depends on a few secrets: JWT signing keys, client secrets, API keys, database passwords. They must never be in source code or committed config files: git history is forever, and repositories get cloned, forked and leaked.
In .NET, configuration is layered, and secrets come in from the outside:
- **Development**: `dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "..."` stores them in your user profile, outside the repo.

- **Production**: environment variables (`Jwt__Key`) set by the platform, or better, a **secret store**: Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes secrets, read at startup with `builder.Configuration`.
- **Best of all, no secret**: managed identities / workload identity let the platform prove the app's identity, so there's nothing to leak.
?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Jwt:Key is not configured.");
Also: rotate secrets on a schedule and immediately after anyone who knew them leaves; use different secrets per environment; scan commits for secrets (GitHub push protection, gitleaks).

steps.prompt: Acceptable place for a production JWT signing key?
items: Azure Key Vault, read at startup
An environment variable set by the hosting platform
A Kubernetes secret mounted into the pod

steps.title: Logging without leaking
body: Logs are copied to many places, kept for months, and read by many people. A bearer token in a log line is a working credential for whoever reads it.
- `Authorization` headers, cookies, API keys, refresh tokens, passwords, one-time codes
- full JWTs (even if expired: they reveal claims and help offline cracking of weak secrets)
Do log: who (`sub`, client id, key **prefix** or id), what, when, the outcome, and a request id. That's what incident responders need.

Defend in depth: don't log request headers by default, use structured logging with named fields, and run a **redaction** step that masks anything that looks like a credential, in case something slips through.

steps.prompt: A simple redactor. What does this print?
steps.explain: `(?i)` makes it case-insensitive. Note the last line: the replacement text normalises the case.

steps.prompt: Complete the redaction of `name=value` secrets in a query string.
steps.explain: Group 1 is the parameter name, kept so the log still says *which* secret was there.

steps.prompt: An incident responder needs to find every request made with a leaked API key. What should the logs contain?
options: The key's id or short prefix, never the full key
The full key, so it can be searched
Nothing about the key at all
The SHA-256 of the client's password

steps.prompt: A secret was committed to git and removed in the next commit. What must happen?
options: Rotate the secret: it lives on in the history and every clone
Force-push to hide the commit, and keep the secret

steps.title: A log redactor
prompt: Write `string Redact(string line)` that masks credentials in a log line:
1. `Bearer <token>` or `Basic <value>` (any case) -> keep the scheme word as written, replace the value: `Bearer [REDACTED]`.
2. Any JWT-shaped text (`eyJ` + base64url, dot, base64url, dot, optional base64url) -> `[JWT]`.
3. `password=`, `secret=`, `api_key=`, `token=` (any case) up to `&` or whitespace -> `name=[REDACTED]`, keeping the name as written.
Apply them in that order. Everything else stays exactly as it was.
hints: Use `Regex.Replace` with a `MatchEvaluator` (`m => m.Groups[1].Value + " [REDACTED]"`) so the original word is kept.
template: Dojo.Eq("a bearer header", "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] path=/me", Redact("Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhZGEifQ.sig_123 path=/me"));
Dojo.Eq("basic auth, lower case", "auth=basic [REDACTED]", Redact("auth=basic dXNlcjpwYXNz"));
Dojo.Eq("a bare JWT", "token in body: [JWT] end", Redact("token in body: eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJzdWIiOiJhZG1pbiJ9. end"));
Dojo.Eq("token= parameter", "refresh token=[REDACTED] ok", Redact("refresh token=8xLOxBtZp8 ok"));
Dojo.Eq("harmless lines are untouched", "user=ada status=200 ms=12", Redact("user=ada status=200 ms=12"));
Dojo.Eq("words that merely contain 'token'", "tokens issued: 4", Redact("tokens issued: 4"));
